**Solution 2 (∞) is wrong.** Its vector fields are not symmetries. For a field X = a(y₁₂,y₁₃)∂_{y₁₂} + b(y₁₂,y₁₃)∂_{y₁₃}, the bracket [X, e₁] has ∂_{w} components equal to −e₁(a) and −e₁(b). In exponential coordinates e₁ = ∂_{x₁} − (x₂/2)∂_{w₁₂} − (x₃/2)∂_{w₁₃} + …, so e₁(a) = −(x₂/2)a_{y₁₂} − (x₃/2)a_{y₁₃}. Since D is spanned by fields with independent ∂_{x_i} components, [X, e_i] ∈ D forces e_i(a) = e_i(b) = 0 for all i. That requires a and b to be constant, so only a 2-dimensional family survives. The infinite-dimensional claim fails.

**Solution 3 (21) is unsupported.** Its B₃/P₁,₂ model has nilradical graded by (4,3,1) under the natural grading, and the other gradings I tried do not give (3,3,2). The solution also contains a self-correction ("24 — wait") and no verification.

**Solution 1 (29) is not verifiable here.** Its stabilizer g₀ has dimension 7, which is consistent with the pencil e₁⊗Ann(e₁) (the stabilizer of the line ⟨e₁⟩ in gl(3) has dimension 7). The symbol brackets also satisfy Jacobi. However, the positive-degree dimensions (6,3,3,2), the total 29, and the claim that this is the global maximum over all pencils and over the (3,6,7,8) case are asserted rather than checked. I could not confirm the prolongation computation or the classification, so I cannot establish that 29 is the correct maximum.

None of the three answers can be confirmed as correct, and two are clearly flawed.

CHOICE: NONE
